clue.text: Studies unauthorised publication of plot

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn, so studies gives cons
piracy is the publishing of someone's work without permission

explanation.surface: Someone looks into the leaking of a storyline before it was meant to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'plot' a storyline that has leaked; it is really a secret scheme. 'Studies' is a verb here, giving the old word CONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a secret scheme hatched by several people is a plot.

clue.text: Hood is lower on top of limousine

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that is on another stands above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a cow lows, so it is a lower, one that moos

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A car's folding roof sits further down over the front of a stretch limo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'further down' but must be said to rhyme with 'mower': an animal that lows. 'on' places it above the letter that 'top of' picks.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a monk's habit has a large loose head covering of this name.

clue.text: Record mark

definitions.meaning: to record something is to write it down, to jot it
to mark something is to notice it and pay attention to it

explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses of one word: to write something down, and to observe or heed it.

clue.text: In his study, did he claim to be a headmaster?

definitions.text: In his study, did he claim to be a headmaster?

parts.words: In his study, did he claim to be a headmaster?
parts.note: a headmaster here is someone expert in heads: the practitioner of the discredited science that read character from the bumps of the skull

explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a school head in his office. Read 'headmaster' as a master of heads and 'study' as his field of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: this practitioner studied skulls and professed expertise in reading character from them.

clue.text: Condemn the joint!

definitions.meaning: to criticise someone savagely is to give them a ...
a joint is a cut of meat cooked in the oven, the British Sunday dinner

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: to criticise fiercely, and a cut of meat cooked in the oven.

clue.text: His piece is valuable as an alternative to prayer

indicators.note: the alternative is put next to the prayer, joined on to it

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in Anglican and Catholic services
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A man's writing is prized by people who would rather read it than pray.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'collector's piece' is an item worth having, which is how the first four words define him. 'to' attaches OR, the word for an alternative, to the prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an item prized by such a hobbyist is called his 'piece', meaning something rare and valuable.

clue.text: Over from a spinner

parts.note: a top is a child's toy that spins

explanation.surface: Six balls bowled by a slow bowler in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: an over is six balls and a spinner is a slow bowler. Here 'Over' just means above and the spinner is a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both are prepositions meaning above or on the summit of something.

clue.text: Effectively having one extra side, subsequently, in Test?

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, the test holding the word for subsequently

parts.note: a test of something is a trial of it
subsequently means afterwards, later

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match somehow ends up with an additional team taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match, an international cricket game, is between two sides, so three-sided means one more than usual. 'in' is the container signal, and the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by comparison: talks or agreements normally have two parties, and this adjective means involving three.

clue.text: Reward action in boxing-match

parts.note: a prize is a reward for winning
action is a military word for a battle or fight

explanation.surface: Something exciting to pay punters back at a night of boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a bout fought by professionals for money is one kind of boxing contest.

clue.text: Fats Waller treated for cataracts

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: The jazz pianist Fats Waller has an operation on his clouded eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes cataracts an eye complaint needing treatment; they are really cascades of water. 'treated' rearranges the pianist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a cataract is a large cascade where a river drops steeply.

clue.text: But she was not "The Bohemian Girl'

definitions.text: But she was not "The Bohemian Girl'

parts.words: But she was not "The Bohemian Girl'
parts.note: the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème is a girl among bohemians, yet the opera actually called The Bohemian Girl is a different work, by Balfe

explanation.walkthrough: Two operas are in play: Puccini's La Bohème, whose seamstress heroine is wanted, and Balfe's The Bohemian Girl, whose heroine is Arline.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion: Puccini's seamstress is the best-known girl in an opera about bohemians, though not in the one with that title.

clue.text: Suddenly produce places for putting young cabbage-leaves

parts.note: to spring a surprise on someone is to produce it suddenly
on a golf course the greens are where players putt

explanation.surface: A cook whips out some tender vegetables with a flourish, and finds spots to set them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' reads as placing something down but is the golf stroke, rhyming with 'cutting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British grocer's name for the loose tender leaves of early cabbages picked before a heart forms.

clue.text: Member not yet named to take seat in the Lords, for example

parts.note: one more of a group, not so far mentioned, is another
a seat at a table or in a hall is a place

explanation.surface: A new peer, still without a title, is about to sit in the upper house of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: By tradition MPs in the House of Commons never name the House of Lords in debate but call it by this phrase, and peers return the compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary euphemism: each House at Westminster refers to the other chamber this way rather than by name.

clue.text: Bursting open in garden, heed scenic design

indicators.note: to design something is to fashion or shape it, so the letters before it are reshaped

explanation.surface: Flowers are coming out everywhere, so pay attention to the landscaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in garden' belongs to the definition: this is a botanist's word for a seed pod splitting. 'design' is an imperative verb here, telling you to refashion the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the splitting of a ripe seed pod or anther to release its contents.

clue.text: It holds the house together

parts.note: the house is a theatre's audience, and they all sit together in one part of the building

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mortar or a beam. In the theatre 'the house' is the audience, as in 'a full house'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: the part of a theatre where the whole audience sits.

clue.text: It's boiling, over, but Nellie is doing the cooking!

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the two words before it are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A pan is bubbling over on the stove while Nellie is in charge of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is doing the cooking' rearranges BUT NELLIE. The comma in the definition is there for the surface: read it as 'boiling over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal Latin sense: the word comes from a verb meaning to bubble up, and now describes someone overflowing with high spirits.

clue.text: Activity of sleeper, perhaps, under cover?

definitions.text: Activity of sleeper, perhaps, under cover?

parts.words: Activity of sleeper, perhaps, under cover?
parts.note: a sleeper is a secret agent planted long before being used, and working under cover means working in disguise

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is someone tossing about beneath the bedclothes. A sleeper is also a spy planted in advance, working under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: spying is what an undercover agent does.

clue.text: Old English chariot race?

parts.note: a race can be a people or tribe, and Queen Boudicca's tribe in Roman Britain is remembered for its war chariots

explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a people, not a contest: the tribe of East Anglia whose queen Boudicca fought the Romans from a chariot.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: an ancient British tribe famous for fighting from chariots.

clue.text: Sign of severe cold? Here's some topping stuff

definitions.meaning: when it is cold enough, frozen water builds up on surfaces such as aircraft wings
the sugar coating spread on top of a cake; topping is also dated British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone with a terrible sniffle is offered something splendid to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the forming of frost on a surface, and the sugar coating of a cake.

clue.text: Standard chart features a short passage

indicators.note: what features something has it inside, so the two pieces together hold the letter

parts.note: par is the standard or expected level, as in below par
a graph is a chart plotting figures

explanation.surface: A routine diagram includes a brief corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' is a verb here, saying the two-word run has the article inside it. The passage is a piece of text, not a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a brief section of prose set off by a new line.

clue.text: Short race, paradoxically

parts.note: someone who is short with you is cross, curt and bad-tempered
a race is a people or nation, a country

explanation.surface: A running event that is brief, though you would not expect it to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is both a piece of the wordplay and the definition. 'paradoxically' admits the joke: this kind of running event is anything but short.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a long run over fields and open ground is one kind of running contest.

clue.text: Chemical can returned to engineers

indicators.note: one piece is brought to the other, so they sit side by side
returned means sent back, so the word for a can is read backwards

parts.note: a can of food is a tin in British English
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A drum of some substance is sent back to the people who built the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TIN into NIT, and 'to' joins it to the army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is the old name for potassium nitrate, also called saltpetre.

clue.text: Artist supporting party given by Mrs Copperfield

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: a do is British slang for a party
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter lends a hand at a soirée hosted by David's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts RA under DO. In Dickens's David Copperfield she is David's first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary reference: David Copperfield's child-wife in the Dickens novel, née Spenlow.

clue.text: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty

indicators.note: something secret is concealed, so the letters lie concealed inside the name that follows

explanation.surface: The title of James Thurber's story about a daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a real title, so nothing looks like wordplay. 'Secret' says the letters are concealed in WalTER Mitty, and 'Life' is a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a life sentence is one length of time a prisoner may serve.

clue.text: Claw hammer

definitions.meaning: an animal's claw is the horny growth at the tip of a toe
as a verb, to hammer something down is to fasten it with metal pins

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the horny tip of a digit, and to fix something in place with a hammer.

clue.text: Struggled with Scandinavian currency in this old racket

parts.note: to struggle against something is to battle it, so struggled is battled
the öre or øre is the hundredth part of the Swedish, Danish and Norwegian crown

explanation.surface: A crook had trouble with Nordic money in a long-running swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The racket is not a swindle but a bat: the small one used with a shuttlecock in the game that came before badminton.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical term: the small bat used to hit a shuttlecock in the forerunner of badminton.

clue.text: Novel predicament, not using Mendelssohn's fourth (The Italian)

indicators.note: not using some letters means leaving them out of the word for predicament

parts.note: a dilemma is an awkward predicament

indicators.note: the fourth of a word is its fourth letter

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: An unusual problem for an orchestra: playing a programme without Mendelssohn's Italian Symphony, his fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: Mendelssohn's Fourth Symphony really is called the Italian. 'not using' takes D ('fourth' letter of Mendelssohn) and IL out of DILEMMA. 'Novel' is the Jane Austen book.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Jane Austen's 1815 book about a matchmaking heroine.

clue.text: Hitler's living-room in the original style

definitions.text: Hitler's living-room in the original style

parts.words: Hitler's living-room in the original style
parts.note: living-room is taken word for word as room to live in, and the original style means in German, the language in which the Nazi slogan for territorial expansion was coined

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a period sitting room. Read 'living-room' as space to live in, put into Hitler's own language.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal translation: the German term for the extra territory the Nazis claimed their people needed.
